requirement:
A built-in reference displayed under {cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`
MUST render as an unlinked badge whose hover text gives the built-in's full text.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.references.builtin_definitions.book_badge` has one clause: a built-in reference displayed under `requirements.references.book_badges` "MUST render as an unlinked badge whose hover text gives the built-in's full text." It prescribes only rendered output: the badge has no link, and its hover text is the built-in's full text.

It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegating interface. Any renderer that emits an unlinked badge with that hover text meets the clause, however it is built. For example, it could be built in a different function, with a different HTML or Markdown emission path, or with different data structures. The implementation choice is discretionary.

The cited `requirements.references.book_badges` text supplies context only. It mentions Shields.io static badges, but the clause under review does not require them. Its other details, such as help cursor, alt text and linking, are behavioral or presentational.

No structural obligation needs implementation evidence here, so the empty review roots are acceptable. Whether the rendering is tested is a separate, behavioral question.

behavioral: The requirement has two observable obligations. A built-in reference displayed as a book badge must render as an unlinked badge, and its hover text must be the built-in's full text.

`src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[fenced_references_render_their_badge_and_body_and_built_ins_are_unlinked]` covers both obligations:
- **Fenced and inline forms.** It renders fenced `{cite} habeas:util` and `{cite} habeas:coverage`, plus an inline `{cite}` of `habeas:util`.
- **Hover text.** It asserts each badge is a `<span class="habeas-req-badge habeas-req-ref-cite habeas-builtin" title="…"><img` element. The title is `escape_html` of the built-in's full text, taken from `builtin(...).text()`.
- **Unlinked.** It asserts the inline badge contains no `<a ` and the whole output has no `href="habeas`. That covers the unlinked part, in contrast to the linked project badges asserted in the same test.
- **Built-in text.** The tests in `src/builtins.rs` check the built-in text against the documentation. The expected text is therefore the real full text, not just whatever the renderer emits.

`src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_metadata_is_hidden_in_fenced_sections_and_preserved_in_details]` is also marked. It exercises `habeas:util` in the cite-metadata hiding scenarios and is supporting evidence only.

The third built-in, `habeas:validate`, is test-role only and has no book rendering test. Its rendering goes through the same generic `reference_badge` path as the other two. That path has no per-name branching, only a role check. So the two tested built-ins exercise the behavior, and I did not treat this as a gap.

text: :::{req} builtin_definitions.book_badge
A built-in reference displayed under {cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`
MUST render as an unlinked badge whose hover text gives the built-in's full text.
:::{req} book_badges
In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference, inline
or fenced, renders as a Shields.io static badge image, subject to the
citation-only paragraph exception below and the reviewed-passage display under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary.display`.
The badge has meaningful alt text displaying its role and full name, and links
to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links
work across chapters, including nested chapters. Apart from the reviewed-passage
exception, a fenced reference renders its badge followed by its body as Markdown.
Inside any prose-bearing colon-fenced section, top-level paragraphs containing
one or more valid inline `{cite}` references and otherwise only whitespace are
omitted from the chapter. This applies to requirements, examples, definitions,
reference fences, and other prose containers, including nested sections.
Requirement and example detail pages still render those citations.
Citations within explanatory prose, lists or blockquotes, unfenced chapter
prose, and references of other roles retain their usual rendering.
Escaped roles, code, raw HTML, and unresolvable references remain literal.
The original declaration, reference discovery, and authoring inputs retain the
citations.
Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive renders with a badge identifying
its kind and full name; text outside a directive remains literal. Declaration
badge navigation follows {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`.
Badge text remains legible regardless of whether its link has been visited.
A badge link shows a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and may
brighten on hover. Badges may be laid out inline with the surrounding text, a
fenced reference's badge and body may be visually set apart from the surrounding
text as one block, and a built-in's unlinked badge may show a help cursor to
signal its hover text. These badges use the syntax defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`.
